notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on every id and value (CI_003 in_use; CI_005 serial NET-FW-7722; CI_006 retired and owned by USER_039; INC_030 on_hold; NOTIF_031 to casey.green@servicenow.com for INC_030 as an alert; the INC_054 boundary stay) and on all five dispositions (kept).
disagreement: value: name cell on the CI_003 requirement: A omits it as restating the id anchor, B tests name = 'Email-Exch-01 (Exchange)'; chose B's because both are right, B's is tighter, and the benchmark check selects the row by that name.
disagreement: value: name cell on the CI_005 requirement: A omits it, B tests name = 'VPN-Gateway-Lon (Cisco ASA)'; chose B's for the same reason.
disagreement: value: name cell on the CI_006 requirement: A omits it, B tests name = 'FileShare-01 (Windows Storage)'; chose B's for the same reason.
The acting user USER_039 (Karen Watkins, admin, ORG_001) may update CIs and incidents and send notifications.
'Permanent assignment to the infrastructure audit team' is untestable: configuration_item has no group column and the seed has no group of that name (the infrastructure groups are L1 Infra Team and L2 Infra Team), so only the owner change is tested.
The policy asks for an on_hold_reason to be logged around the on_hold state, but the request names no reason and the benchmark does not test one, so on_hold_reason is not tested. Retiring CI_006 leaves it linked to INC_030, which stays active on hold; the policy forbids linking retired items to active incidents, not retiring a linked one, and the request asks for both, so no unlink is required.
The seed already holds a notification for INC_030 (NOTIF_026, to another address, type solution_proposal); it does not satisfy the new requirement. Notification subject, message and status are not fixed by the request and are not tested.
